cands.name: Gerald Baldi
cands.bio: Age 70 per Bradenton Times; former advertising executive who moved into real estate, then financial services and banking; organizer of Indivisible Manatee's regular west Bradenton rallies. Won Democratic primary Aug 18, 2026 (unofficial 66.8% over John Houman). First-time candidate; decided to run mid-March 2026.
cands.local_ties: Manatee County activist (Indivisible Manatee west Bradenton rallies); specific residence/length of residence not found.

record.text: No prior public office or votes. Campaign platform (BallotReady): civil-rights state laws, clean-water and solar cooperatives, infrastructure first with impact studies and district approval before new home building.
Bradenton Times endorsed him in both the Democratic primary and the general, citing his opposition to overdevelopment and state preemption.

endorsements.text: The Bradenton Times editorial board (primary and general).
Endorsed by primary rival John Houman (per BlueVoterGuide listing).

local_issue_stance.text: Platform calls for requiring impact studies and district approval before new home building; Bradenton Times endorsement frames him as against sprawl and state preemption of local decisions.

cands.name: Jim Boyd
cands.bio: Bradenton Republican, Senate Majority Leader and Senate President-designate for the 2026-28 term (chosen unanimously by the GOP caucus Oct 14, 2025). Owns Boyd Insurance & Investments. Born in Bradenton; FSU B.S. 1978; Palmetto City Council 1988-91; North River Fire District commissioner; Florida House 2010-2018; Senate since 2020. Long-time member of the Senate Banking & Insurance committee.
cands.local_ties: Born in Bradenton; Senate bio lists spouse from Palmetto and past Palmetto City Council service; family political dynasty (grandfather and uncle served in Florida House/Senate). Lives in Bradenton (Your Observer). District office 717 Manatee Ave W, Bradenton.

record.text: SB 180 (2025, 'hurricane' bill containing the clause barring local governments in affected counties from adopting more restrictive or burdensome land-development/comp-plan rules and moratoria, sponsor Nick DiCeglie): Boyd voted Yea on Senate passage 4/9/2025 (37-0) and on concurrence 5/2/2025 (34-1; recorded as a Yea cast after roll call). Signed 6/26/2025. Manatee County is among ~25 local governments suing over it.
Vote record PDF for SB 180 Senate passage showing 'Y Boyd-20'.

HB 399 (2026, Land Use and Development Regulations: fee-nexus for permits, as-of-right off-site/manufactured housing, administrative approval for 'large destination resorts', compatibility rules; Chapter 2026-7): Boyd voted Yea on final Senate passage 3/13/2026 (27-11). He voted Nay on Sen. Jones's floor amendment 351666 (failed 17-20). Bradenton Times opinion column calls him a reliable vote in the pro-preemption bloc (opinion).
SB 264 (2023, restricts land purchases by certain foreign-country interests, sponsor Collins): Boyd voted Yea on both the 4/11/2023 Senate passage (38-0) and the 5/4/2023 concurrence (31-8).

Sponsored SB 4-D (2022 special session, Building Safety / post-Surfside condo structural rules): passed Senate 38-0, House 110-0, signed 5/26/2022. Also co-sponsor (with Appropriations) of CS/SB 2-D Property Insurance (2022 special session): Senate 30-9, House 95-14, signed 5/26/2022. In Oct 2025 he said the Dec 2022 property-insurance reforms are 'working' and further changes are 'a little ways out'.

Property tax: voted Yea on CS/HJR 1-F 'Save Our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes' (June 2, 2026; Senate 30-9) which puts a Nov 2026 ballot amendment raising the non-school homestead exemption ($150k in 2027, $250k in 2028); needs 60% voter approval.

Feb 18-19, 2026: filed an amendment to SB 302 (coastal resilience) barring further dredging/filling in the Terra Ceia Aquatic Preserve (exceptions for navigation, stagnant-water clearing and 'minimum dredging' for marinas/ramps/piers); Senate adopted SB 302 38-0; House matched; DeSantis signed 3/19/2026. Widely reported as blocking the proposed Manatee (Terra Ceia) cruise port.
Official Florida Senate page (committees: Banking & Insurance, Fiscal Policy, Regulated Industries, Rules, Joint Legislative Budget Commission; Majority Leader).

money_notes.text: Affiliated political committee: 'Building On Your Dreams Political Committee' (registered 01/27/2021 under Boyd, per Florida Senate lobbying/registration list). TransparencyUSA (Florida DOE data aggregator) lists it as Boyd's largest contributor at $1,950,000; other top contributors named there: Florida Chamber of Commerce PAC, NextEra Energy Capital Holdings Inc, The Southern Group of Florida Political Committee; total contributions shown about $4.9M (cycle/date range not shown in the search snippet; page returned 403 to direct fetch so numbers are from the search result summary only).
Florida Politics reported the committee took in $92,500 in a single month and held about $414,706 cash on hand (date not visible; older reporting).
Registration list showing the committee under Boyd's name.

foreign_ties.text: None documented in the public records searched (FARA filings, foreign-government payments, state-owned business, foreign-agent donors).

endorsements.text: Boyd was unanimously designated Senate President for 2026-28 by the Senate Republican caucus, with praise from current President Ben Albritton. No 2026 group endorsements of Boyd found in searches (Chamber/Realtors/etc. not confirmed).

local_issue_stance.text: Voted Yes on SB 180 and HB 399 (preemption of local land-use rules); Manatee's wetland-buffer rollback and the county's inability to reverse it are tied to SB 180 by local reporting.
Authored the Terra Ceia Aquatic Preserve dredging ban (SB 302 amendment) that blocked the cruise port; says current protections are sufficient but is open to more.
Voted Yea on the property-tax homestead exemption amendment headed to the Nov 2026 ballot.

Same paper's separate column says he voted for SB 840 (a bill to narrow SB 180) that passed the Senate unanimously but died in the House.
